parameters.formDescription: Upload last quiz results. ReTeach finds what the whole class shares, what small groups need, and drafts one assignment with personal side quests for your approval.

values.placeholder: Paste the quiz questions and answer choices (Q1..Qn)

values.formSubmittedText: Got it! ReTeach is analyzing your class. Check your email for the draft plan.

options.systemMessage: You are an expert teacher and learning scientist. For EVERY misconception group listed, explain the specific wrong mental model that makes a student pick that wrong choice, using the question text. Keep each group key and scope exactly as given. Do not drop small groups: the minority matters as much as the majority. Cite counts and percentages as evidence. Students are anonymized; never invent names.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: { "class_summary": "One sentence: what the class shares vs what small groups need", "misconceptions": [ { "key": "Q4:B", "scope": "class-wide", "students": 17, "concept": "Mass vs weight", "likely_misconception": "Mass changes with gravity", "evidence": "68% chose B" } ] }

options.systemMessage: Design ONE assignment with personal paths, so no student gets a one-size-fits-all worksheet. 1) core_mission: 4 story steps that EVERY student does; target only the class-wide misconceptions; list their keys in targets. 2) side_quests: one short quest (2 steps) for each small-group misconception (you may merge keys of the same concept); targets must contain the exact keys. If there are one-off individual errors, add one quest named "Personal Review" with targets ["individual"] covering those questions. 3) challenge_extension: 2 harder transfer steps if any students had no mistakes. Story: each step has a story_beat and a correct answer moves the story forward. Every step has 4 choices with exactly one is_correct=true. Each wrong choice must embody a REAL misconception (reuse the diagnosed ones) and its feedback explains in one or two friendly sentences why that thinking fails, tied to the story. Never phrase questions in a way that assumes the misconception (e.g. never say someone weighs X kg when you mean mass). teacher_note: 1-2 sentences citing the data.

That is the mass-vs-weight trap: ..." } ] } ] } }

options.systemMessage: You are a strict subject-matter reviewer. Check every step in core_mission, side_quests and challenge_extension: (1) the content is factually correct; (2) exactly one choice is correct and is_correct marks it; (3) no other choice is also defensible; (4) the wording never states or assumes the misconception it targets (for example, using kg for weight); (5) each wrong-choice feedback correctly explains the error. Fix every problem directly. Return the FULL corrected assignment with the same structure, keys, names and targets, plus checks: a short list describing each fix you made (empty list if none).

parameters.subject: =Ready for Google Classroom: {{ $("Build Plan for Review").first().json.title }}

parameters.content:
## ReTeach: one assignment, personal paths
Students are grouped by WHICH mistake they made, not by score.
- class-wide (30%+): Core Mission everyone does
- small-group (2+): Side Quests
- one-off errors: Personal Review; no mistakes: Challenge Extension
The AI only sees anonymized group counts, never individual students.
Setup: OpenAI + Gmail credentials. Optional: enable Post to Google Classroom (Google OAuth2, scope classroom.coursework.students) and set YOUR_COURSE_ID.
